messages:
alex: Quick flag — p95 spiked ~12% on mixtral-moerouter canary last night after the kernel-selector tweak. Noticed correlation with high top-k routing tails.

maria: Oof. Do we have a perf trace? was it for long seqs or short ones?

alex: Short/medium seqs (~512) primarily. I pulled a perf flame from the canary host: top hotspots are:
```
- kernel_dispatch_dispatcher::select_kernel 28.4%
- expert_forward_batching::apply_kv_cache 17.1%
- softmax_topk_router::compute_logits 14.6%
- rope_scaling::rotate_heads 9.7%
- cudnn/matmul (various) 8.9%
```
Seems the selector picked the new 'mixed-rope-optimized' kernel, but that kernel's internal path does an extra reshape for kv dims when head_dim != 64, adding copies.

jin: Interesting — any recent model config changes? head_dim/kv_dim tweaks?

alex: Yes, for Mixtral-7B-MoE we switched to head_dim=80 for a better RoPE alignment in a prior PR. That likely made the kernel hit the slow path.

sam: That would explain the rope_scaling hit. When head_dim != power-of-two multiples we fall into a copy/pack slow path.

maria: Also saw elevated KV cache eviction rate on the same hosts. Cache stats:
```
- cache_capacity_entries: 1.2M
- eviction_count_1h: 83k (baseline 9k)
- avg_kv_lookup_latency_ms: 0.42 -> 1.3
```
Cache thrashing + extra copies = higher p95.

opsbot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-17T23:40 reverted due to p95 regression alert.

alex: Right. Reversion happened. Need plan: either revert kernel-selector tweak permanently or add guard to avoid mixed-rope kernel when head_dim != 64/128 multiples.

jin: Before we revert, can we test a hybrid mitigation: force top-k routing to a dedicated expert-pool that uses fallback kernel (the older kernel) for those sequences? That keeps throughput intact for others.

maria: We can try a routing policy change: route requests with seq<=768 and topk>=4 to fallback pool. Quick patch in router policy.

sam: Also consider lowering router temperature (softmax temp) by 0.1 for canary so topk distribution narrows — reduces expert fan-out and cache pressure.

alex: Good call. Proposed immediate steps:
- A1 (maria): push router policy rule for canary -> route small seq & high-topk to fallback pool.
- A2 (jin): add kernel-selector guard to skip mixed-rope kernel for head_dim not in {64,128} (hotfix).
- A3 (sam): tweak router temp by -0.1 in canary config.
- A4 (alex): run perf harness with reproducer and capture kernel-level traces + nvtx markers.

maria: I'll open canary PR now. I can target just the canary hosts and include the routing rule.

jin: I can push the guard as a feature-flagged change (off by default). Will run local unit + microbench for head_dim 64 vs 80.

sam: I'll change temp in the rollout config and monitor expert fanout 10m windows.

alex: Repro steps for A4 (if anyone wants to run locally):
```
# reproduce load pattern
./scripts/loadgen --model mixtral-moex --seq 512 --topk 6 --qps 120 --duration 600 
# perf capture (on canary instance)
perf record -F 99 -g -- ./mixtral_server --config /etc/mixtral/canary.yaml
# nvprof / nvtx around hot path
```

maria: Added the PR: router: canary-policy -> { if seq<=768 && topk>=4 -> pool=fallback-kernel } . Patch link: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4521

sam: After patching router, expert fanout 10m sample dropped from median 22 -> 9, cache eviction rate halved. Early numbers look promising.

jin: Local microbench results for selector guard: head_dim=80 path was 21% slower on mixed-rope kernel vs fallback. Guard + fallback kernel eliminated that delta. I'll mark the guard for canary-only rollout.

alex: Nice. Any kernel-level suggestions long-term?

sam: We should:
- Add pack-friendly codepaths in mixed-rope kernel to avoid copies for non-power-of-two head dims.
- Teach kernel-selector to consider kv_cache_eviction_estimate + expert_fanout_pred when choosing kernel (cost-model).

maria: Also add a batching heuristic tweak: limit continuous micro-batches sent to same expert if its local queue latency > 30ms; that prevents the hot expert from getting overloaded and causing cross-host evictions.

opsbot: ci-bot: Canary PR passes tests; rolling config to 3 nodes now.

alex: Good. Action owners: maria (router rule deploy), jin (selector guard), sam (router temp + batching heuristic), alex (perf trace + follow-up kernel ticket). I'll open follow-up kernel ticket for long-term work.

maria: Deployed canary rule. Monitoring dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/d/xyz/mixtral-canary — watching p95 and eviction counts.

sam: After all three changes are live on the canary, p95 regressed back within baseline (within 2%) and eviction_count_1h is ~11k.

jin: I'll keep the selector guard flagged for 48h then we can decide. I'll also produce a microbench matrix across head_dim in {64,72,80,96,128} and seq lengths {128,256,512,1024}.

alex: Awesome. If canary remains stable, we can ship a safer kernel-selector with the cost-model and batching heuristics next sprint.

sam: FYI, recorded a small patch to the router to emit per-request nvtx id so we can correlate kernel traces to router-decisions later. PR queued.

maria: Thanks all. Tagging @oncall to keep an eye for any fallout. :thumbsup:

opsbot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout completed to 3 nodes (changes: router-rule, temp adjustment).

alex: Will check dashboards in the morning. Good work team.
